problem: An agent adds each new file to the nearest folder, and no test rewards a better place. The coach reports smells inside one file only. The VALIDATE rubric scores behaviour only. In some sessions the main agent writes the slice itself, so no coach and no blind score run.
why_now: The research synthesis of 2026-11-10 found that guidance at the start lowers the first level of decay, not its rate. Feedback during the write had the best evidence. The coach and the blind rubric already run in the slice loop.
approach: One stdlib script, shared/structure_signals.py, holds three signals that need no parser: a crowded folder, a name-stem cluster, and a generic file name. A signal fires only for a file that is untracked or added since the merge-base. One config file, .cobuilder/structure-signals.json, holds each limit. The coach gives GREEN the signals for each file extension, as advice that names the decision. The GREEN filter stays. VALIDATE writes an advisory Structure block and judges contract drift. The main agent spawns the three agents, and a script checks one effect. A replay decides what the rubric scores.

alternatives.option: Build a new /architect:refactor command with a graph engine, as the first research run proposed
alternatives.rejected_because: It runs after the damage. The evidence favours feedback at write time, and its thresholds have no source.

alternatives.option: Remove the GREEN filter, so the coach runs for each caller in each session
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-0025 holds the filter as a rule. Each write in each session then waits on habit-hooks. The engineer kept the filter.

alternatives.option: Add weighted structure criteria S1 to S5 to the rubric at once
alternatives.rejected_because: The rubric has no weights, and a score is a plain average. An unproven threshold can then fail a slice.

alternatives.option: Keep a baseline file of old findings in .cobuilder/
alternatives.rejected_because: A git comparison with the merge-base, with untracked files included, gives the same ratchet. It adds no state file to keep current.

alternatives.option: Add an import check with dependency-cruiser and import-linter in the first version
alternatives.rejected_because: It adds two tool dependencies and covers two languages only. The three signals work in each language.

alternatives.option: Add a PreToolUse speed bump that blocks the first write of a new file
alternatives.rejected_because: It is a fifth hook script and a new event under ADR-0025. No study shows that a block works better than advice.

alternatives.option: Make slice-loop.js the default way to run each slice, so code enforces the agent order
alternatives.rejected_because: It is too heavy for a small build, and each run needs the engineer to opt in. Code cannot enforce agent use in each session.

alternatives.option: Show agent use with a marker that the coach hook writes
alternatives.rejected_because: The coach ignores each caller except GREEN. A missing marker then means a main-agent slice or a silent coach, and the check cannot tell them apart.

alternatives.option: Silence the coach on the habit-hooks markers for an unscanned file
alternatives.rejected_because: For a scanned extension, those markers show a misconfiguration that GREEN must report. The guard keys on the file extension instead.

alternatives.option: Run the script from the coach with uv run, and read a YAML config
alternatives.rejected_because: The coach is stdlib only, and two coach tests fail when it runs uv. A uv start on each write also adds delay.

alternatives.option: Deliver the signals as a sensor in a project-local habit-hooks plugin
alternatives.rejected_because: habit-hooks finds smells inside one file, and the signals judge folders and names. The engineer keeps the two jobs apart. A sensor also runs for six extensions only.

out_of_scope: A scored structure criterion in the rubric, which the replay evaluation of E5 decides
An import check against the forbidden_dependencies of a boundary.yaml
A PreToolUse speed bump for a new file
A change to the GREEN filter of the coach
A claim about who wrote the code, a human or an agent
risks: The coach message grows with no cap, and noise hides the smell advice. A cap is added only if the replay or the engineer finds noise
A percentile limit gives false signals in a framework folder, a test folder, or a generated folder
GREEN splits a folder to silence the signal, and the new folders hold no single decision
The coaching language does not change what GREEN does, so the engineer reviews it before the coach uses it
The advisory Structure block has no effect on GREEN, because only a failed attempt passes it on
Neither text nor the effect check forces the main agent to spawn the agents. The check finds a skipped agent only after the slice
The stem rule flags a test folder, where files share a prefix such as test_ by convention
testing: Tests run the script on synthetic folder trees and read its JSON. A stub-binary test drives the coach. A blind pass scores the loop text, and the transcript is kept. The replay evaluation compares folder growth and the follow-on resolve rate.
reviewer_focus: The spike first: one real coach message from the second runner, and the agent-use effect
The effect that shows which agent wrote a slice. The hook must not call the tracker, and a coach marker cannot work
The percentile limit and the generic-name list, which have no calibration data
unknowns: Whether one runner call on each write adds a delay that GREEN notices
Whether the structure findings need a cap, which the replay and the engineer decide
Which effect shows that the agents ran the slice. The candidates are the VALIDATE attempt file and the tracker attempt record. The spike decides
Which repositories and slice plans the replay uses, and how many runs the engineer accepts
Whether the signals must serve target repositories in each language, which the engineer has not confirmed
Why the main agent skipped the agents in past sessions, because no transcript of such a session was read
How a check finds a partial skip, where the main agent writes the code and spawns only VALIDATE. Neither candidate effect shows it
